answer: An agent network resists Sybils through bonded capital tiers structured like a terrace. Each agent must lock a 500-token security bond for ninety days to graduate beyond a zero-weight trial tier. A Sybil attacker creating fifty fake nodes must lock 25,000 tokens upfront, scaling capital costs linearly while per-identity voting influence remains capped. Low-tier nodes cannot access the consensus haven or manipulate quorum. If coordinated manipulation is detected, validators slash the entire bonded pool into a shared lotus treasury, making Sybil replication strictly negative-sum.
